learn.title: Resistance
learn.body: Resistance is how much a part opposes current. It is measured in ohms, written $\Omega$. With the same voltage, more resistance means less current. A resistor is a part made to have a set resistance.

learn.title: Ohm's law
learn.body: Voltage, current and resistance are linked by $V=IR$. Rearranged: $I=\frac{V}{R}$ and $R=\frac{V}{I}$. Use volts, amps and ohms together. Cover the one you want and the other two show how to find it.

learn.title: Find the current
learn.body: A 12 V supply is across a 4 ohm resistor.

learn.title: Find the voltage
learn.body: 0.5 A flows through a 20 ohm resistor.

learn.title: Power
learn.body: Power is how fast energy is used. It is measured in watts (W). $P=VI$. A part with 12 V across it and 3 A through it uses $12\cdot 3=36\ \text{W}$.
Check your units. Volts, amps and ohms go together. Convert mA to A first.

questions.prompt: 6 ohms across 12 V. What is the current in A?
3 A flows through 4 ohms. What is the voltage in V?
10 V drives 2 A. What is the resistance in ohms?
The voltage stays the same and the resistance doubles. What happens to the current?
questions.explanation: $I=\frac{V}{R}$, so a bigger $R$ gives a smaller $I$. Doubling $R$ halves $I$.
From $V=IR$, divide both sides by $I$ to get $R=\frac{V}{I}$.

questions.prompt: 5 V and 2 A. What is the power in W?
Match each formula to the quantity it gives.
questions.explanation: Each formula is the same law arranged to find a different quantity, plus power.
